2609.26758.title: Type-Safe Is Not Error-Free: A Constrained Decision Head Follows the Option Name, Not the Rubric Bound to It
2609.26758.paper_summary: Typed decision models are built for settings where model outputs are consumed directly by software. Instead of generating free-form text, they return a decision over a predefined set of options. By construction, every output conforms to the required schema. Yet this guarantee does not tell us whether the model interprets the options as intended. We study Jev and two Jev-like models with open weights by changing how option names are assigned to rubrics. Each option consists of an option name and a textual rubric that defines what the option means. We change only which option name is assigned to each rubric; the question, state, rubric wording, and set of option names remain exactly the same. On 1200 workflow decisions with task-specific rubrics, renaming the two options from 0/1 to no/yes changes 70.4 more answers per hundred (95% CI: [67.6, 73.1]) and shifts AUC from .94 to .23, revealing a systematic reversal in the decision ranking rather than simple uncertainty. The same operation has little effect with neutral option names. This pattern holds across all 4 predicates, where the effect is at least 7.4x larger than under the neutral control, and becomes stronger as the number of options increases. The effect also depends on the read-out geometry: a second model family that mean-pools over the full option span flips 4.1x less often. The hosted model exhibits the same behavior: the swap changes AUC from .8146 to .5806 and produces 24x as many answer flips as its test-retest floor. In contrast, replacing the option names with random character strings returns all model families to the neutral-control regime without reducing accuracy. The failure therefore depends on the semantic polarity of the option names rather than on the renaming operation itself. Across all conditions, the type-error rate remains 0%, even when decision accuracy degrades substantially.
2609.26758.paper_summary_zh: 打字決策模型是為了在模型輸出直接被軟體消耗的情境而建立的。它們不是生成自由形式的文本，而是返回一個預定義選項集合中的決策。從結構上講，每個輸出都符合所需的架構。然而，這一保證並不能告訴我們模型是否按照預期解釋這些選項。我們研究了Jev和兩個類似Jev的開放權重模型，通過改變選項名稱分配給評分標準的方式。每個選項由一個選項名稱和一個定義該選項含義的文本評分標準組成。我們僅改變分配給每個評分標準的選項名稱；問題、狀態、評分標準措辭和選項名稱集合保持完全相同。在1200個具有任務特定評分標準的工作流程決策中，將兩個選項從0/1重新命名為no/yes使每百個答案的變化增加了70.4個（95% CI: [67.6, 73.1]），並將AUC從0.94轉變為0.23，顯示出決策排名的系統性逆轉，而不是簡單的不確定性。對於中性選項名稱，這一操作幾乎沒有影響。這一模式在所有4個謂詞中都成立，效果至少比中性控制大7.4倍，且隨著選項數量的增加而變得更強。該效果還取決於讀出幾何：第二個模型族在整個選項範圍內進行均值池化，翻轉的頻率降低了4.1倍。託管模型表現出相同的行為：這一交換使AUC從0.8146變為0.5806，並產生了24倍於其測試-重測基準的答案翻轉。相對而言，用隨機字符字符串替換選項名稱使所有模型族回到中性控制範疇，而不降低準確性。因此，這一失敗取決於選項名稱的語義極性，而不是重命名操作本身。在所有條件下，類型錯誤率保持在0%，即使決策準確性大幅下降。
2609.26758.author: Yu Sun et.al.
